title: Prometheus
tagline: They went looking for our makers. We just made dinner.
about: A science crew follows an ancient star map to a distant moon, hoping to meet the beings who made us.
cue: Serve the snacks when the crew stumble out of two years in stasis and Vickers drops for push-ups.
faces: Weyland Corporation flight to LV-223. Meals served after stasis

    StartersIsle of Skye smoked salmon oatcakesOatcakes topped with lemon and dill crème fraîche, smoked salmon, capers and cracked pepperHow to make it150g crème fraîche1 lemon1 bunch dill16 oatcakes200g smoked salmon slices1 tbsp baby capers, drainedcracked black pepper, to tasteZest the lemon. Mix the crème fraîche with the zest, a squeeze of lemon juice, a tablespoon of chopped dill and pepper.Spread over the oatcakes and top each with a fold of salmon, a few capers and a dill sprig. Finish with cracked pepper.Janek's Christmas tree pigs in blanketsChipolatas wrapped in streaky bacon, roasted with a honey and wholegrain mustard glaze and rosemaryHow to make it12 pork chipolatas6 rashers of streaky bacon2 tbsp honey1 tbsp wholegrain mustard1 tbsp olive oil2 sprigs of rosemaryHeat the oven to 200°C. Cut the bacon in half lengthways and wrap a strip around each chipolata. Lay on an oiled tray, seam side down.Mix the honey and mustard.Roast for 15 minutes.Brush with the glaze and roast until sticky and browned.Pull the rosemary into small sprigs and use them to spear each one.Hummus with warm flatbreadVickers's pick, from the food stores in her private module.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsChristmas Day landfall beef WellingtonSeared beef eye fillet in mustard, prosciutto and thyme mushroom duxelles, baked in golden puff pastryHow to make it800g beef eye fillet, centre cut1 tbsp vegetable oil2 tbsp Dijon mustard500g button mushrooms2 garlic cloves25g butter1 tsp thyme leaves8 slices of prosciutto2 sheets of frozen puff pastry, thawed1 egg, beatensalt and pepper, to tasteSeason the beef well with salt and pepper. Sear in the oil in a hot pan until browned all over, then brush with the mustard.Blitz the mushrooms and garlic to a fine crumb. Cook in the butter with the thyme until all the liquid has gone and it holds together. Season.Cool the beef and mushrooms completely.Overlap the prosciutto on a sheet of cling film, spread with the mushrooms, sit the beef on top and roll up tightly in the film. Chill to firm.Heat the oven to 210°C. Join the pastry sheets, unwrap the beef onto it and wrap, trimming the excess and sealing the seams underneath. Brush with egg and score the top.Bake on a hot tray until deep golden, about 35 minutes for medium rare.Rest before cutting into thick slices.David's Lawrence of Arabia chickenDavid, alone on the ship for two years, bleaching his hair to look like Peter O'TooleHow to make it8 chicken thighs, bone in2 tsp baharat spice2 tbsp olive oil1 lemon300g basmati rice1 pinch saffron30g butter50g pistachios50g dried cranberries1 parsley200g Greek yoghurt1 garlic cloveRub the chicken with the baharat, oil, lemon juice and salt and roast at 200°C for 40 minutes until crisp.Soak the saffron in 2 tbsp hot water. Simmer the rice with 600ml water, covered, for 12 minutes, rest for 5, then stir through the saffron and butter.Fold the chopped pistachios, cranberries and parsley through the rice.Mix the yoghurt with the crushed garlic and a pinch of salt.Serve the chicken on the jewelled rice with the garlic yoghurt.SweetsBlack goo chocolate potsRich dark chocolate baked custards, chilled and topped with crème fraîche and blackberriesHow to make it200g dark chocolate, 70 percent, chopped300ml thickened cream100ml full cream milk3 egg yolks40g caster sugarsalt, a pinch100g crème fraîche125g blackberriesHeat the oven to 150°C. Chop the chocolate into a heatproof bowl.Heat the cream and milk until steaming and pour over the chocolate. Stir until smooth.Whisk the yolks, sugar and salt, then whisk in the chocolate cream. Strain into 4 ramekins and sit them in a deep tray. Pour hot water halfway up the sides.Bake until set at the edges with a wobble in the middle.Lift out of the water and cool.Chill until set.Top each pot with a spoon of crème fraîche and a few blackberries.DrinksHolloway's spiked nightcapScotch whisky shaken with honey syrup and lemon over ice, with a dark drop of blackcurrantHow to make it60ml honey60ml hot water240ml Scotch whisky3 lemons, juiced to make 80ml4 tsp blackcurrant cordial3 cups iceStir the honey into the hot water until dissolved, then cool.Juice the lemons.Shake the whisky, honey syrup and lemon juice hard with half the ice.Strain into 4 tumblers over the rest of the ice and let a teaspoon of blackcurrant cordial sink into each.
